questions.q: Which of the following scenarios violates the concept of heat flow?
options: Ice melts in a warm room
A hot pan cools on a metal counter
A cold spoon becomes colder when placed in hot soup
Warm air rises from a radiator
questions.explanation: A cold spoon must gain heat from hot soup and become warmer. Becoming colder would mean heat flows from cold to hot, which is impossible.

questions.q: Two beakers contain equal mass of water. Beaker A is at 40°C. Beaker B is at 20°C. You add the same amount of heat to both. Which will have a higher final temperature?
questions.explanation: Equal mass and substance means each beaker rises by the same ΔT. A started higher (40 + ΔT) than B (20 + ΔT), so A stays higher.

questions.q: A scientist says: "Two objects in contact reached the same temperature, but heat continues to flow." Is this possible?
options: No, heat stops when temperatures equal
Yes, if they are in vacuum
questions.explanation: Thermal equilibrium means no net heat flow. When temperatures are equal, heat stops flowing on average.

questions.q: Which unit is used for both heat energy and other forms of energy like work?
questions.explanation: Joule (J) is the SI unit for all forms of energy, including heat, work, kinetic energy, etc.

questions.q: A 100 g iron nail at 200°C is dropped into 1 kg of water at 25°C. The final temperature is 26°C. What can you conclude?
options: Water gained more heat than iron lost
Iron lost more heat than water gained
Heat lost by iron = heat gained by water
Temperature of iron did not change
questions.explanation: Law of conservation of energy: heat lost by hot object = heat gained by cold object (assuming no heat loss to surroundings).

questions.q: A clinical thermometer reads 40°C. The patient's actual temperature is 39°C. What could have caused this?
options: The thermometer was not shaken before use
questions.explanation: If the previous reading was 40°C and the thermometer was not shaken to reset it below 35°C, it will still show 40°C even if the patient is cooler.

questions.q: Two thermometers — one with mercury and one with alcohol — are placed in the same water. Mercury rises to 70°C. Alcohol rises to 70°C as well. What can you conclude?
questions.explanation: Both thermometers are calibrated correctly. If both show the same reading, that is the actual temperature.

questions.q: At what temperature do Celsius and Fahrenheit scales show the same number?
questions.explanation: Solve C = (C × 9/5) + 32 → C − (9C/5) = 32 → (5C−9C)/5 = 32 → (−4C)/5 = 32 → C = −40. At −40°, both scales read the same.

questions.q: A laboratory thermometer has 10 divisions between 30°C and 40°C. What is the least count?
questions.explanation: Range = 10°C. Number of divisions = 10. Least count = 10/10 = 1°C.

questions.q: Why is alcohol sometimes used instead of mercury in very cold regions?
options: Alcohol freezes at −115°C, mercury freezes at −39°C
questions.explanation: In extremely cold places like Siberia, temperatures can drop below −40°C. Mercury would freeze, but alcohol remains liquid.

questions.q: A metal rod is heated at one end. After some time, the other end becomes hot. Which statement correctly describes the process?
options: Particles move from hot end to cold end
Particles vibrate and pass energy to neighbors
Hot air carries heat along the rod
questions.explanation: In conduction, particles do not move from place to place; they vibrate and transfer energy through collisions.

questions.q: A room has a radiator near the ceiling. The room does not warm up well. Why?
options: Hot air stays at ceiling and does not reach floor
questions.explanation: Heaters should be placed near the floor because hot air rises. If placed near ceiling, hot air stays up and cold air stays down.

questions.q: Which surface is best for absorbing radiant heat?
questions.explanation: Dull black surfaces are the best absorbers of radiation. Shiny surfaces reflect radiation.

questions.q: On a cold night, a glass window feels colder than the wooden door frame even though both are at the same temperature. Why?
options: Glass conducts heat away from your hand faster
questions.explanation: Glass is a better conductor than wood. It pulls heat from your hand faster, making it feel colder.

questions.q: In which of these situations is heat transferred primarily by radiation?
options: Frying an egg on a pan
Warm air rising from a desert
Feeling heat from a campfire from 5 meters away
An iron rod in a furnace
questions.explanation: At a distance, conduction and convection are negligible. Radiation from the fire travels directly to you.

questions.q: A student touches a metal rod and a wooden rod that have been sitting in a freezer at −10°C. Which statement is correct?
options: The metal rod feels colder because it conducts heat faster
The wooden rod feels colder because it stores more cold
Neither feels cold because the room is warm
questions.explanation: Metal conducts heat away from the hand faster than wood. "Cold" is the sensation of heat leaving your body.

questions.q: A house in a desert has thick mud walls. The mud walls keep the inside cool during the day and warm at night. Why?
options: Mud is an insulator with high thermal mass
questions.explanation: Mud is a poor conductor (insulator). It heats up slowly during the day and cools down slowly at night, reducing temperature swings. This is called "thermal mass" or "thermal inertia."

questions.q: Which combination of materials would make the BEST thermos flask to keep coffee hot for 12 hours?
options: Metal inner + metal outer + no vacuum
Glass inner + glass outer + vacuum + silver coating
Plastic inner + plastic outer + air layer
Copper inner + copper outer + black coating
questions.explanation: Vacuum stops conduction and convection; silver coating reflects radiation; glass is also a poor conductor. This is exactly how a real thermos works.

questions.q: Why are electrical wires that carry current covered with plastic or rubber?
options: Plastic and rubber are insulators that prevent electric shock and heat loss
questions.explanation: Plastic and rubber are electrical and thermal insulators. They prevent electric shock and also prevent heat from escaping (or entering) the wire.

questions.q: In a traditional Japanese house, floors are covered with tatami mats (made of rice straw and rush grass). Why do these mats feel warm to bare feet in winter even though the room is cold?
options: The mats are good insulators and prevent heat loss from feet
The mats are good conductors and bring heat from the ground
The mats are at a higher temperature than the air
questions.explanation: The mats are insulators, so when you step on them, your body heat does not flow away quickly. They feel warm because heat is trapped near your skin.

questions.q: A coastal city has a temperature of 35°C at 2 PM. An inland city at the same latitude has 42°C. Which is the most likely reason?
options: Sea breeze cools the coastal city
Land breeze cools the coastal city
questions.explanation: Sea breeze brings cool ocean air to coastal city during afternoon, reducing temperature compared to inland.

questions.q: Which statement about land breeze is TRUE?
options: It occurs when land is warmer than sea
It occurs only during full moon
It occurs when sea is warmer than land
It blows from sea to land
questions.explanation: Land breeze occurs at night when sea is warmer than land, so wind blows from land to sea.

questions.q: A student claims: "Sea breeze is stronger in summer than in winter." Is this correct?
options: Yes, because temperature difference is larger in summer
No, sea breeze is stronger in winter
Sea breeze does not occur in summer
Sea breeze strength is same all year
questions.explanation: In summer, land becomes much hotter than sea, creating a large temperature difference → stronger sea breeze.

questions.q: Why does land heat up faster than water? (Choose the BEST reason.)
options: Water has higher specific heat capacity and mixing currents
Land is closer to the Sun
questions.explanation: Water has high specific heat (takes more energy to warm) and also mixing currents distribute heat downward.

questions.q: At 6 AM on a beach, the air temperature over land is 18°C and over sea is 22°C. Which direction will the wind blow?
questions.explanation: Land (18°C) is cooler than sea (22°C). Cooler air over land is denser and flows towards warmer sea → land breeze.

questions.q: Two rods — one made of steel and one made of brass — are exactly the same length at 20°C. They are heated to 100°C. Which rod will be longer? (Steel expands less than brass.)
questions.explanation: Brass has a higher coefficient of thermal expansion than steel, so it expands more for the same temperature increase.

questions.q: A concrete sidewalk has gaps every few meters. In summer, the gaps almost disappear. In winter, they become wider. Why?
options: Concrete expands in summer, contracts in winter
Concrete contracts in summer, expands in winter
Gaps fill with dirt in summer
The sidewalk moves due to earthquakes
questions.explanation: Concrete expands when hot (summer), closing the gaps; contracts when cold (winter), widening the gaps.

questions.q: A metal ball has a diameter of 5.00 cm at 20°C. Its coefficient of linear expansion is 0.000019 per °C. What is its approximate diameter at 120°C?
questions.explanation: Expansion = original length × coefficient × ΔT = 5 × 0.000019 × 100 = 0.0095 cm. New length = 5.0095 cm.

questions.q: Why does a tightly closed glass bottle filled completely with water sometimes crack when left in a freezer?
questions.explanation: Water expands as it freezes (anomalous expansion). The expanding ice exerts pressure on the glass, causing it to crack.

questions.q: A thermostat uses a bimetallic strip to turn a heater on and off. As the room cools, the strip straightens and completes an electrical circuit. Which metal is on the outside when the strip is bent in a warm room?
questions.explanation: In a warm room, the bimetallic strip is bent. The metal with higher expansion is on the outside of the bend (longer arc). As the room cools, the strip straightens.

questions.q: 10 g of ice at 0°C is mixed with 100 g of water at 30°C. The final temperature is 20°C. What can you conclude?
options: Ice melted completely and then water warmed
The experiment was done in a vacuum
questions.explanation: The final temperature is above 0°C, so all ice melted. The ice absorbed latent heat to melt and then sensible heat to warm to 20°C.

questions.q: Why does a pressure cooker cook food faster than an open pot?
options: Higher pressure increases latent heat of vaporization
Higher pressure raises boiling point, so food cooks at higher temperature
Pressure cooker is made of metal
questions.explanation: Higher pressure means water boils at >100°C. Higher cooking temperature means faster cooking.

questions.q: Which statement about latent heat is TRUE?
options: Latent heat can be measured with a thermometer
Latent heat causes temperature to rise
Latent heat is absorbed or released during state changes without temperature change
Latent heat only applies to water
questions.explanation: This is the definition of latent heat. Temperature remains constant during the state change.

questions.q: A cold drink has ice cubes floating in it. After 10 minutes, the ice cubes have melted but the drink temperature is still 0°C. Where did the heat to melt the ice come from?
questions.explanation: The drink (liquid) was above 0°C initially. It gave up its heat to melt the ice, cooling itself down to 0°C in the process.

questions.q: You have two identical burners. You put 1 kg of ice at 0°C on one and 1 kg of water at 0°C on the other. Which will reach 100°C first? (Both receive same heat per second.)
questions.explanation: Ice must first absorb latent heat (334,000 J) to melt into water at 0°C, then heat from 0°C to 100°C. Water at 0°C only needs to heat from 0°C to 100°C. The water wins by 334,000 J worth of time.
